ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Figure 17 shows the Gulf of Mexico and its surrounding areas, with New Orleans marked near the north shore of the Gulf of Mexico. On the right side of the figure there are latitude labels of 0° and 23°26′; New Orleans is located north of these low latitudes and belongs to the Northern Hemisphere range. The question stem states that “New Orleans is due north of the hurricane center.” Reasoning: A Northern Hemisphere hurricane is a low-pressure vortex; near-surface winds rotate counterclockwise around the hurricane center and converge toward the center. If New Orleans is due north of the hurricane center, then the tangential wind of the counterclockwise circulation there is roughly westward, while the component converging toward the low-pressure center is southward; the resultant actual wind direction is blowing toward the southwest. In meteorology, wind direction is named according to where the wind “comes from,” so a wind blowing toward the southwest comes from the northeast direction; therefore New Orleans blows a northeast wind.

method.method_draft: 先读图确认新奥尔良在墨西哥湾北岸、位于北半球；再读题给出的条件“新奥尔良位于飓风中心正北”。把飓风视为北半球低压涡旋：风围绕中心逆时针并向中心辐合。位于中心正北的地点，风的实际运动方向合成为向西南吹；按气象上风向以“来向”命名，因此新奥尔良吹东北风。

推理：北半球飓风是低压涡旋，近地面风围绕飓风中心逆时针旋转，并向中心辐合。若新奥尔良在飓风中心正北，则该处逆时针环流的切向风大致向西，同时向低压中心辐合的分量向南，合成的实际风向是向西南吹。气象上风向按风“从哪里来”命名，因此向西南吹的风来自东北方向，所以新奥尔良吹东北风。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This route uses the pressure-gradient/Coriolis force balance to construct the wind direction, rather than starting from the memorized counterclockwise-spiral description of a hurricane.
planner_metadata.image_role: Use 图17 to ground the geographic hemisphere: New Orleans is shown on the Gulf Coast above the equator/near the tropics, so the Coriolis deflection should be treated as Northern Hemisphere deflection.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the textual condition that the city is exactly north of the hurricane center; no other numerical data from the text is needed.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For a low-pressure hurricane, air tends to move toward the low-pressure center; in the Northern Hemisphere moving air is deflected to its right by the Coriolis force, producing a wind that crosses inward with a rightward-deflected component. At a location north of the low center, the inward pressure-gradient direction is southward; right deflection gives a westward component, so the flow is toward southwest. Since wind direction is named by the source direction, that is a northeast wind.
